pages.text: Auntie Gyamea was cooking morning porridge, stirring it steadily with a long wooden spoon. Habiba watched from the kitchen doorway, keeping well back from the hot stove just as Auntie had taught her.
sentences: Auntie Gyamea was cooking morning porridge, stirring it steadily with a long wooden spoon.
Habiba watched from the kitchen doorway, keeping well back from the hot stove just as Auntie had taught her.
pages.alt: From a safe kitchen doorway, Habiba watches Auntie Gyamea stir porridge in a pot on the stove with a long wooden spoon.

pages.text: Auntie rested a metal spoon in the pot for a moment, and when she lifted it out she held a folded kitchen cloth around it. “Why did you use the cloth?” asked Habiba. “A metal handle quickly grows hot,” said Auntie, “whereas a wooden handle stays cool.”
sentences: Auntie rested a metal spoon in the pot for a moment, and when she lifted it out she held a folded kitchen cloth around it.
“Why did you use the cloth?” asked Habiba.
“A metal handle quickly grows hot,” said Auntie, “whereas a wooden handle stays cool.”
pages.alt: Auntie Gyamea holding a shiny metal spoon safely with a thick folded cloth in one hand and a cool wooden spoon in the other as Habiba watches from the doorway.

pages.text: “Let us test that safely at the table using warm tap water, never hot water,” said Auntie. She poured warm tap water into a sturdy mug. Habiba placed one metal spoon and one wooden spoon into the water and waited five minutes.
sentences: “Let us test that safely at the table using warm tap water, never hot water,” said Auntie.
She poured warm tap water into a sturdy mug.
Habiba placed one metal spoon and one wooden spoon into the water and waited five minutes.
pages.alt: At a wooden dining table well away from the stove, Habiba places a metal spoon and a wooden spoon side by side into a mug of warm water while Auntie Gyamea smiles.

pages.text: After five minutes, Habiba touched the top of each handle gently. The metal handle felt noticeably warm, while the wooden handle still felt cool. “The warmth travelled right up the metal,” she said, “yet it did not travel up the wood!”
sentences: After five minutes, Habiba touched the top of each handle gently.
The metal handle felt noticeably warm, while the wooden handle still felt cool.
“The warmth travelled right up the metal,” she said, “yet it did not travel up the wood!”
pages.alt: Habiba gently touching the upper tips of the metal spoon handle and wooden spoon handle in the mug on the table, looking amazed.

pages.text: “Exactly,” said Auntie Gyamea. “Metal lets heat pass through easily, whereas wood does not. That is why many cooking pots are made with wooden or heat-safe plastic handles, and why cooks love wooden stirring spoons.”
sentences: “Metal lets heat pass through easily, whereas wood does not.
That is why many cooking pots are made with wooden or heat-safe plastic handles, and why cooks love wooden stirring spoons.”
pages.alt: At the kitchen table, Auntie Gyamea points out the sturdy wooden side handles on an empty, cool cooking pot beside a wooden spoon.

pages.text: “And remember our home rule,” Auntie added firmly. “Children never touch a hot pot or go near a lit stove—grown-ups handle the cooking.” Habiba nodded, carried the test mug to the basin, and washed her hands.
sentences: “And remember our home rule,” Auntie added firmly.

pages.alt: Habiba washing her hands with soap at a clean washbasin while Auntie Gyamea looks on warmly beside the tidy table.

activities.definition: Energy of warmth that moves from warmer things to cooler things.

The part of a spoon, tool, or pot made to be held in the hand.
